title: Quantum transmission in 1D disordered stealthy hyperuniform Kronig--Penney-like models
authors: Shaobing Yuan, Carlo Vanoni, Salvatore Torquato
abstract: Disordered stealthy hyperuniform (SHU) systems are emerging as platforms for controlling classical and quantum transport due to vanishing single-scattering contributions in the stealthy regime. Here, to our knowledge, we present the first perturbation theory of one-dimensional quantum transport through a continuum of identical point scatterers with SHU positional disorder. Our perturbation theory indicates the exact cancellation of all the lower-order terms due to the Fourier-space stealthy condition $S(q)=0$, and the further suppression of the lowest non-vanishing fourth order in the Lyapunov exponent $λ(k)$ due to the real-space hyperuniform constraint $\lim\limits_{D\to\infty}σ_D^2=c<\infty$. Our findings presents universal implications of the general wave-propagation phenomena in disordered SHU systems.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes quantum transport in 1D disordered systems exhibiting stealthy hyperuniformity. By developing a high-order perturbation theory, the authors show that the SHU condition causes the leading localization effects to vanish up to the third order. This demonstrates that structural order can parametrically enhance quantum transmission, leading to a much weaker, fourth-order dependence on disorder strength.
main_problem: The paper investigates quantum transmission and localization in one-dimensional disordered systems characterized by 'stealthy hyperuniform (SHU)' disorder.
main_result: The SHU condition causes the leading attenuation of the Lyapunov exponent to vanish up to the third order in the scattering strength, shifting the leading localization dependence to the fourth order ($O(W^4)$).
method: The authors employ advanced perturbative quantum field theory techniques, utilizing Feynman diagrams to calculate the Lyapunov exponent and inverse lifetime in the thermodynamic limit.
model_or_system: The model is a Kronig-Penney-like system describing quantum particle propagation through a continuum of identical point scatterers in 1D, governed by a delta-function potential.
key_observables: Lyapunov exponent ($\lambda(k)$), transmission $T(E)$, inverse lifetime ($1/	au(k)$), and the structure factor $S(k)$.
important_parameters: The scattering strength ($W$), the wave vector ($k$), and the hyperuniformity cutoff ($K$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on taking the thermodynamic limit ($N 	o \infty$) and making specific approximations for summing over momenta in the perturbative expansion.

paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the perturbative calculation of the Lyapunov exponent and inverse lifetime, first for free boundary conditions, and then adapts the formalism for periodic boundary conditions, culminating in the analysis of the SHU regime.
why_interesting: The systematic, high-order perturbative calculation provides deep insight into how specific geometric constraints (hyperuniformity) can fundamentally alter the scaling of quantum localization, which is a core topic in condensed matter theory.
